summary.text: A seamount is a large undersea landform, typically an extinct volcano, that rises from the ocean floor without reaching the surface.
Seamounts are so numerous that they form one of the most common marine ecosystems, attracting plankton, corals, fish and marine mammals.
More than 14,500 have been identified, but only a few have been studied in detail, and ships have even collided with uncharted ones.

facts.label: Minimum height
facts.value: At least 1,000 m above the surrounding seafloor

facts.label: All combined
facts.value: A landform the size of Europe

facts.label: Fishing damage
facts.value: 95% of ecological damage from bottom trawling

items.prompt: If every known seamount were gathered into one place, about how big would the landform be?

options.label: The size of a large city
The size of a small island
The size of Europe
The size of the Moon

items.explain: All known seamounts collected into one area would make a landform the size of Europe.

items.prompt: Fishing fleets often work the waters right above seamounts. Why?

options.label: The water there is always warmer
Currents and the raised peak draw in sea life
Nets never snag on the rocky bottom
Sunlight reaches all the way to the summit

items.explain: Interactions with currents and their elevated position attract plankton, corals and fish, and many seamounts support extensive fisheries.

items.prompt: As a seamount ages, material seeping into it puts pressure on its sides. What can that eventually lead to?

options.label: Landslides that can set off huge tsunamis
A sudden rise until it becomes an island
A steady leak of fresh water into the sea
A slow change into a coral reef

items.explain: Pressure on the flanks causes landslides that can generate massive tsunamis, the greatest danger from seamounts.

items.prompt: A big seamount grows up to the surface, waves wear its summit level, and then it sinks again. What is it now called?

options.label: An atoll
A trench
A ridge
A guyot

items.explain: After they subside below the surface, such flat-top seamounts are called guyots or tablemounts.

items.prompt: The Emperor Seamounts northwest of Hawaii were built by volcanoes millions of years ago. What has happened to them since?

options.label: They have grown into new islands
They have melted back into magma
They have sunk far below sea level
They have drifted into the Arctic

items.explain: Formed by volcanism millions of years ago, the Emperor Seamounts have since subsided far below sea level.

items.prompt: Why are most seamounts found on ocean crust near mid-ocean ridges, mantle plumes and island arcs?

options.label: Currents pile sediment there
Most of them began as volcanoes
The water there is shallowest
Coral grows fastest in those spots

items.explain: Most seamounts are volcanic in origin, so they tend to sit near ridges, mantle plumes and island arcs.
